metadata.title: Claude, Canva Creator.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether a Skill named canva-creator lets Claude design anything in Canva or something narrower, using the skill's own template constraint as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that it fills a fixed template, the same way every time, and has nothing to fall back on once a request steps outside it.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B03 (the template card - filling it holds, stepping outside it fails)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Canva Creator lets Claude design anything from scratch. It doesn't — it works from a fixed template. So here's the real question: it designs from a template, right?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude, Canva Creator — it designs from scratch, right?', hesitates on 'scratch', corrects to 'a template', lands the real question

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('scratch' -> 'a template') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A Claude Skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is canva-creator — for turning a request into a finished Canva design. Its SKILL.md is the full instruction set, plain language, no hidden logic — and it plants one constraint early: match an existing template, don't design a new one.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR PLANTED — a folder, a file, a fixed template

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR PLANTED — a folder, a file, a fixed template
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon labelled 'canva-creator' opens to reveal a SKILL.md card. Its text scrolls briefly, then one line highlights in terracotta: 'match the template.' A template card locks into a frame beside it. THIS EXACT TEMPLATE CARD RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The instructions run top to bottom. Claude reads one step, does it, then reads the next — no branching unless a step calls for it. Feed it a business name, a color palette, and the words for a flyer, and it walks that same fixed sequence every time.

shot.new_visual_element: A numbered step list lighting up in order, no branch lines

production_viz.label: One line, no branches
production_viz.mechanic: Three small input cards — business name, color palette, flyer copy — feed in at the top. Below them, a numbered vertical list of steps lights up one at a time as a small arrow travels straight down the chain. No branch lines anywhere.

beats.narration_text: Here's the template again: fill in your text, your colors, your logo, and Claude drops them into the layout the file describes. Stay inside that template and the result is consistent, every run. Ask for something the template doesn't cover — a different shape, a layout nobody wrote — and the skill has nothing to reach for.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same template card, filled and then mismatched

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — fits, then doesn't
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 TEMPLATE CARD RETURNS, identical. Text, a color swatch, and a logo mark drop into its fixed slots one by one; the card brightens green when full. Then a request shaped like a different layout arrives at the same card — it has no matching slot, nothing lights, and the card stays as it was.

beats.narration_text: canva-creator fills in a fixed template, the same way every time. Step outside that template, and it has nothing to fall back on.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me: 'I want to turn our event flyer into a Canva design, using our shop's colors and logo. Read the canva-creator skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it.' Watch whether it names the template it's filling in before it starts — that's the constraint from this reel, right there on screen. Liam, in for Bear.
